items.text: The Dalí Museum in St. Petersburg, Florida, is home to over 2,400 works by Salvador Dalí. Dalí was a famous surrealist painter who mixed real and dream-like images. He once said he would never die, and in a way, his art keeps him alive. The museum has a special show, Dalí Alive 360, where visitors can feel surrounded by his work. Classical painting and the ideas of Sigmund Freud inspired Dalí and his paintings. His famous melting clock painting is in New York, but many other pieces are in Florida because two collectors, Elanor and Reynolds Morse, loved his work and gave their collection to the city. The museum opened in 1982 and now welcomes over 300,000 visitors each year. Dalí’s art still amazes people today. Difficult words: surrealist (dream-like style), surrounded (having things or people around), amaze (to make someone be surprised or wondering). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Dalí Museum in Florida has many paintings and sculptures by Salvador Dalí. Dalí is a famous artist who paints in a dream-like way. He lives in the 20 th century. He once says that he will never die. And his art is still here today. The museum has a special show where people can feel inside his paintings. Dalí learns to paint like old artists but wants to make something new. His famous melting clocks painting is in New York, but many of his works are in Florida. A couple, Elanor and Reynolds Morse, give their collection to the city. The museum opens in 1982 and now many people visit. Dalí’s art is still exciting and important today. Difficult words: sculpture (the art of making objects of metal, stone, wood, or glass), melting (turning into a liquid form), collection (a group of things such as paintings, old objects, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Denmark is introducing compulsory military service for women two years earlier than planned. Women turning 18 after July 1st, 2024, could be drafted from 2026 onwards. Both men and women must now participate in an annual ballot , with names drawn if there are not enough volunteers for the army. Additionally, Denmark has extended military service from four to eleven months. In response to the growing threat from Russia, the country has also increased its defense budget by 6.8 billion euros. While compulsory service for women is rare in Europe, Sweden introduced it eight years ago, and Norway, a NATO member, did so ten years ago. Other countries like Latvia and Lithuania are considering similar measures. Many European nations had suspended conscription after the Cold War, but Russia’s annexation of Crimea and the war in Ukraine have changed this. Germany, for example, faces a shortage of soldiers but would need a constitutional change to introduce mandatory service for women, a politically challenging move. Difficult words: ballot (voting), conscription (mandatory military service), annexation (taking over a territory). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Denmark is making military service mandatory for women two years earlier than planned. Women who turn 18 after July 1st, 2024, may join the army from 2026. Men and women must now take part in a lottery, and if there aren’t enough volunteers , the lottery will decide who will join the army. Denmark also extended military service from four to eleven months. The country is increasing military money by 6.8 billion euros. Few European countries have mandatory service for women, but Sweden and Norway do. Other countries like Latvia are thinking about it. Many European nations stopped mandatory military service after the Cold War, but with the war in Ukraine, some are thinking about it again. In Germany, changing the law for women’s service would be very difficult. Difficult words: mandatory (when a law says that you must do something), volunteer (a person who freely offers to do something), extend (to make longer or larger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Denmark will start military service for women. It will happen earlier than the government plans. Women who turn 18 after July 1st, 2024, may have to join the army from 2026. Men and women will now be part of a lottery . If not enough people ask to join, the lottery will choose them. Denmark also makes military service longer, from four to eleven months. The country is spending more money on the military because of the war in Ukraine. Not many European countries make women join the army, but Sweden and Norway do. Other countries like Latvia are thinking about it. Many countries stop military service after the Cold War, but now some are bringing it back. Germany may find it hard to do the same. Difficult words: military service (army training which young people must do in some countries), join (to become part of), lottery (choosing people or things by chance). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

World Athletics has introduced mandatory cheek swabbing to confirm the gender of athletes competing in the female category. The organization’s president, Sebastian Coe, stated that this measure is necessary to protect female sports and ensure fair competition. The tests will start at the World Championships in Tokyo in September. A testing provider is currently being selected, and the procedure will only be required once in an athlete’s career. Coe emphasized that maintaining the integrity of women’s sports is a priority. He stated that World Athletics has been working on this issue for years and has defended its regulations in court. The decision has led to discussions about whether other sports federations might adopt similar measures. This topic is widely debated, with some critics arguing that such testing could become invasive . While World Athletics insists the tests are non-invasive, past gender testing methods have been controversial. The issue of fairness and inclusion in sports remains a significant concern for international sports organizations. Difficult words: mandatory (something that must be done), swab (a small medical test), invasive (causing discomfort or harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

World Athletics decided that athletes must take a cheek swab test to check their gender before competing in the female category. The president, Sebastian Coe, said this is important to protect women’s sports and make sure competitions are fair. The first tests will happen at the World Championships in Tokyo in September. The organization is looking for a company to do the tests. Each athlete will only take the test once in their career . Coe said World Athletics worked on this for many years. Some people believe other sports may also start using these tests. Some people think the tests may be uncomfortable. World Athletics says they are simple and not painful, but some worry they could become more difficult. The discussion about fairness in sports continues. Difficult words: swab (a small medical test), career (the job or jobs that you do during your working life), fairness (when things are right and equal for everyone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

World Athletics will check the gender of athletes who want to be in the female category. Athletes must take a test. The president, Sebastian Coe, says this is important to keep women’s sports safe and fair. The first tests will happen in Tokyo in September. The organization is finding a company to do the tests. Athletes will take the test only once. Coe says that this is an important rule . Maybe other sports will also start using these tests. Some people do not like this rule. World Athletics says the tests are easy. They do not hurt. But some people are worried about them. Difficult words: gender (whether you are a man or woman), female (a woman), rule (what you must or must not do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The nightclub scene in the UK has been affected by changes in society. Many clubs closed after the pandemic, and the cost of living has made it more difficult for people to go out. As a result, many young people now prefer spending time in cheaper places like bars instead of expensive nightclubs. Alcohol consumption has also dropped among younger generations, which has led to a decline in traditional clubbing. Some venues have changed their business models, offering events like quiz nights or alcohol-free spaces to attract people. Independent venues are adapting to these changes and thriving by creating more inclusive and affordable environments. For example, a club in Sheffield provides a space for queer people and others who feel marginalized . These places are often nonprofit and focus on community. Despite the challenges, nightclubs and independent spaces remain an important part of youth culture, and many believe these places should be protected. Difficult words: queer (a word that describes people who are not heterosexual), marginalized (treated as less important or less valued), nonprofit (an organization that doesn’t make money for individuals). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many nightclubs in the UK closed after the pandemic because of money problems. Young people don’t go out as much because it is expensive. They now like to go to bars or other places that cost less money. Some people drink less alcohol, so they don’t need to go to nightclubs. Some nightclubs changed by offering fun activities like quiz nights or spaces where people don’t drink alcohol. Some small clubs are doing well because they focus on being friendly to everyone, for example, LGBTQ+ people and others. These clubs focus on creating good community experiences. Even with problems, nightclubs and small spaces are still important for young people and music lovers. Difficult words: LGBTQ+ (a community of people with different sexual orientations), focus (to give attention to). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many nightclubs in the UK close. They do not make enough money. Young people do not go to nightclubs as much because it is too expensive . They go to cheaper places like bars. Some people drink less, so they do not want to go to nightclubs. Some nightclubs change by having quiz nights or places where people do not drink alcohol. Some small clubs work well because they help all people, for example, LGBTQ+ people. These clubs are important for young people and music lovers. Difficult words: expensive (when something costs a lot of money), quiz (a game with questions), LGBTQ+ (a group of people with different sexual feelings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis has returned to the Vatican after spending five weeks in hospital due to double pneumonia . The 88-year-old pope faced a serious health crisis, with complications that made it the most difficult challenge of his 12-year papacy. Doctors say that even though the pope has left the hospital, he will need about two months of rest to fully recover. During this time, he must avoid large meetings and stressful situations. Despite his health issues, Pope Francis made a public appearance on Sunday, smiling and waving at well-wishers, although he used a wheelchair and appeared frail . His face was swollen, and he had bandages on both arms. He thanked a woman who had visited him daily during his hospital stay. The pope’s doctors mentioned that it would take time for him to fully regain strength and voice. Difficult words: pneumonia (a lung disease), frail (weak), regain (to get something back). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pope Francis came back to the Vatican after staying in hospital for five weeks because of pneumonia . The 88-year-old pope had serious health problems. Doctors say he will need two months of rest to recover fully. After leaving the hospital, he appeared in public, smiling and waving at people. He was in a wheelchair and looked weak. His face was swollen, and he had bandages on his arms. He thanked a woman who had brought flowers for him while he was in hospital. Pope Francis also had problems with his voice because of the long illness. Doctors said it would take time for him to feel better. Difficult words: pneumonia (a lung disease), recover (to get better after an illness), bandage (a piece of cloth which you wear around an injury). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis is in the Vatican after staying in hospital for five weeks. Pope Francis is in hospital because of a lung disease called pneumonia. He is 88 years old and had a lot of health problems. Doctors say he needs two months to rest . After leaving the hospital, he waves and smiles at people. He uses a wheelchair . He looks weak . He thanks a woman who brings flowers for him. His voice is weak because of his long illness. Doctors say that it will take time for him to feel better. Difficult words: rest (to relax), wheelchair (a chair to transport a person who cannot walk), weak (not strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ecopetrol, Colombia’s largest oil company, has polluted hundreds of sites, including water sources and wetlands, according to a BBC investigation. Leaked data shows over 800 cases of oil pollution from 1989 to 2018, with about 20% not reported. The company denies wrongdoing, stating that it follows environmental laws. A whistleblower Andrés who worked as an adviser to the CEO discovered severe water pollution and hidden reports of oil spills. He shared confidential data with journalists, exposing violations of environmental laws, including unreported spills. After revealing this information, he received death threats and was forced to leave Colombia. The oil industry in Colombia is linked to armed conflicts, with security companies possibly hiring former paramilitaries . Environmental activists and critics of Ecopetrol face serious threats, and Colombia remains one of the most dangerous countries for them. Despite the risks, Andrés continues to work on climate policies from exile in Germany. Difficult words: whistleblower (a person who reports illegal or dishonest activities), paramilitary (a group of armed people not officially part of the military), exile (being sent away from your own country, especially for political reasons). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ecopetrol, a big oil company in Colombia, pollutes many places, including rivers and wetlands. A former worker found secret reports of oil spills from 1989 to 2018. The company never reported some of them, but it says it follows the law. Andrés worked for Ecopetrol and saw harmful water pollution. He shared this information with journalists. After this, he got death threats and had to leave Colombia. The oil industry in the country has problems with violence . Security companies sometimes work with dangerous groups. People who speak against Ecopetrol are often in danger. Many received threats, and some were even killed. Andrés now lives in Germany and works to protect the environment. Difficult words: former (existing in the past), death threat (when someone promises to kill a person), violence (hurting people and causing damage). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ecopetrol is a big oil company in Colombia. It makes many places dirty with oil, like rivers and wetlands . A worker finds secret information about oil spills . Ecopetrol does not speak about some of them. The company says it follows the rules. Andrés sees dirty water and tells people about it. Later, he gets messages which scare him. He must leave Colombia. It is not safe for him to stay. The oil industry in Colombia has problems with bad people. People who talk about pollution are not safe. Some get scary messages, some even die. Andrés lives in Germany now. He works to help the natural world. Difficult words: wetland (a large area of land with lots of water in it), oil spill (when oil gets into the sea or river), pollution (dirty water, air, or land). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US government recently released classified documents related to the 1963 assassination of President John F. Kennedy. President Donald Trump announced the release of 80,000 new pages, adding to the six million pages already available. Jefferson Morley, a journalist and JFK assassination researcher, argues that recent findings challenge the official story that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone. According to Morley, doctors in Dallas believed Kennedy was shot from two directions, and the CIA knew much more about Oswald than they admitted. He claims the Warren Commission misled the public, and new documents may reveal the CIA’s role in monitoring Oswald before the assassination. Some believe national security concerns are an excuse to hide embarrassing details. While politicians from both parties push for full disclosure , many questions remain unanswered. Researchers hope these newly released files will provide a clearer picture of what happened on November 22, 1963. Difficult words: classified (secret), mislead (to cause someone to have a wrong idea or impression), disclosure (making information public). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US government released secret documents about the 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy. President Trump announced 80,000 new pages, but many are not online yet. Journalist Jefferson Morley says new information proves that the official story of Lee Harvey Oswald acting alone is false. Doctors believed that the shooting happened from two directions, and the CIA secretly watched Oswald before the attack. Morley says the CIA hid and still hides important details. The agency says releasing all information could harm national security, but many people think they only want to keep a good reputation . Politicians want the full truth. Researchers hope these new documents will tell us more about the events of November 22, 1963. Difficult words: release (to make something available), prove (to show that something is true), reputation (what people think of someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US government shares new secret papers about President John F. Kennedy’s death in 1963. There are six million pages about the killing. President Trump is releasing 80,000 pages. Some experts say that these papers may show that the official story is wrong. Many people believe that Lee Harvey Oswald does not act alone. Doctors say that the shooting happens from two sides. Some people believe that the CIA knows a lot about Oswald before the killing. The CIA keeps some papers secret. They say that it is for security. But many people think they are hiding something. People hope that these new documents will tell the full truth about the killing. Difficult words: secret (when many people do not know about something), release (to make something available), hide (to keep something away from others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy cautiously welcomed a proposed limited ceasefire with Russia but emphasized the need for more details. He is willing to stop attacks on energy infrastructure if Russia reciprocates . His comments followed a call between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Despite these discussions, Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure continued. Zelenskyy accused Russia of prolonging the war, while Putin rejected Washington’s push for a full 30-day ceasefire, demanding an end to Western military aid as a condition for peace. Trump denied that Putin had made such a demand. Russia agreed to halt attacks on Ukraine’s energy sector for 30 days, but other targets remain vulnerable . Talks between US and Russian officials in Saudi Arabia should continue, but deep divisions remain, as Russia insists on stopping foreign aid while Ukraine refuses to make territorial concessions . Difficult words: ceasefire (an agreement to stop fighting to allow discussions about peace), reciprocate (to do the same), vulnerable (able to be easily attacked or influenced), concession (compromise). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy says he is open to a small ceasefire with Russia but wants more details. He agrees to stop attacks on Russian energy sites if Russia does the same. He said this after US President Trump spoke with Russia’s President Putin. Russia still attacked Ukraine even after the call. Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to delay the war. Putin refused a full ceasefire and said he wanted Western countries to stop sending guns to Ukraine first. Trump, however, said Putin never asked for this. Russia agreed not to attack Ukraine’s energy facilities for 30 days, but other areas are still in danger. Ukraine does not fully trust this deal, and new peace talks will happen soon, but both sides strongly disagree. Difficult words: ceasefire (stopping fights for a time), delay (to make something take longer), refuse (to say no). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy wants to stop fighting with Russia for a short time but needs more information. He will stop attacks on Russia’s energy places if Russia stops too. He says this after a talk between US President Trump and Russia’s President Putin. But Russia still attacks Ukraine after the talk. Zelenskyy thinks that Russia wants to make the war last longer. Putin says that he will not stop fighting if the West helps Ukraine. Trump says that Putin does not ask for this. Russia will not attack Ukraine’s power stations for 30 days, but the situation in other places is still dangerous . People in Ukraine do not believe Russia. More talks will happen soon. Difficult words: power station (a place which produces electricity), dangerous (not safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Union is discussing ways to support Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) after the Trump administration cut its funding. RFE/RL has been an essential source of information since the Cold War, broadcasting in 27 languages across 23 countries, including Ukraine, where it covers Russian-occupied territories. Last Friday, after Congress passed a government funding bill, Trump ordered reductions to several agencies, including the US Global Media Agency, which funds RFE/RL. The network’s president, Stephen Capus, warned that cutting support would benefit America’s adversaries . The Czech Republic, where RFE/RL has operated for 25 years, is leading the effort to secure new funding. Czech Foreign Minister Jan Lipavský has urged the EU to intervene . Sweden also supports financing the network, emphasizing its importance for democracy. However, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said securing funding would be difficult, as many organizations require financial aid. However, EU ministers are determined to find a solution to keep RFE/RL operating. Difficult words: adversary (an enemy), intervene (to take action to help), determined (firmly decided). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The EU is trying to help Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) after the US stopped funding it. RFE/RL is important for sharing news since the Cold War. It broadcasts in 27 languages and reports on places like Ukraine, where it covers Russian-occupied areas. Last Friday, Donald Trump ordered funding cuts, which affected RFE/RL. The head of the network, Stephen Capus, said this would help America’s enemies . RFE/RL started working in the Czech Republic 25 years ago. The Czech government wants the EU to give money to support it. Sweden agrees and says the network helps democracy. Some leaders say that it is hard to find money because many groups ask for help. Still, EU ministers want to find a way to save the network. Difficult words: funding (money for a project), broadcast (to transmit a program or some information by radio or television), enemy (a person who hates or fights with someone else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US stops giving money to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL). The EU wants to help. RFE/RL gives important news. It works in Prague, the Czech Republic, since the Cold War. It speaks 27 languages. It reports in Ukraine, where Russia takes some land. Last Friday, Donald Trump stops some funding . The boss of RFE/RL, Stephen Capus, said this helps America’s enemies . The Czech Republic wants the EU to help RFE/RL. Sweden also says the radio is important to keep countries and people free. An EU leader, Kaja Kallas, said finding money is difficult because many groups need help. But EU ministers want to try. Difficult words: report (to give information about something), funding (money for a project), enemy (somebody you fight with). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brisbane may lose the tennis matches for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games to Melbourne if the city does not improve its facilities, warns Tennis Australia. Tennis Queensland has proposed a 113-million-dollar plan to upgrade the Queensland Tennis Centre, including a new 3,000-seat arena and eight new courts. Currently, the venue doesn’t meet the required standards for the Games, so Tennis Queensland is asking for additional government funding. Without funding, the tennis events might be moved to Melbourne. Tennis Queensland’s CEO, Cameron Pearson, explained that the state lacks enough courts, seating, and proper player facilities. He expressed hope that the government would support infrastructure improvements. The Queensland government is set to announce the final infrastructure plan by March 25. Queensland’s Tourism Minister has also emphasized the importance of creating long-term benefits from the Games, while some in Melbourne have suggested they could host the tennis matches. Difficult words: standard (a level of quality), lack (to be without or not have enough of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brisbane may lose the tennis matches for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games if it doesn’t improve its facilities . Tennis Queensland needs 113 million dollars to upgrade the Queensland Tennis Centre. The plan includes building a new 3,000-seat arena and adding eight more courts. The current facilities are not big enough. If the government doesn’t give money, the tennis events could be moved to Melbourne. Tennis Queensland’s CEO, Cameron Pearson, says there are not enough courts or seating for the Games. The government will announce its decision about the facilities by March 25. Some people in Melbourne say their city has better sports facilities and could host the tennis matches. Queensland’s government wants to make sure that the state will benefit from hosting the Games in the future. Difficult words: facility (the building, equipment, or service needed for a particular activity), upgrade (to change something for something newer or better), announce (to tell people about something officially). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brisbane may lose the tennis matches for the 2032 Olympic Games if it does not improve its courts. Tennis Queensland wants 113 million dollars to build a bigger arena and more courts. The current place is not big enough. If the government does not give money, the tennis matches may take place in Melbourne. Tennis Queensland says there is not enough space or seating in Brisbane. The government will decide what to do by March 25. Some people in Melbourne say that their city has better courts. Melbourne could hold the tennis matches. The government in Queensland wants to make sure the state will get good things from hosting the Games. Difficult words: improve (to make something better), arena (a large place for sports events), host (to hold an event). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethiopia and Eritrea, former enemies, may be on the brink of war again, according to regional officials. This conflict would destroy the peace agreement that earned Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019 and could worsen the humanitarian crisis in the Horn of Africa. Tensions rose after the 2020-2022 civil war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region, where Eritrea supported Ethiopia’s federal army against the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). However, the peace deal signed in 2022 excluded Eritrea, leading to a split between Ethiopia and Eritrea. A faction in Tigray recently took control of Adigrat, which increased instability in the region. Both Ethiopia and Eritrea have deployed troops, raising concerns of direct conflict. Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after years of war. The two nations fought again in 1998 but reconciled in 2018. However, their relationship deteriorated after Ethiopia’s peace agreement with the TPLF. Eritrea is also alarmed by Ethiopia’s growing interest in gaining sea access. Difficult words: faction (a small group within a larger group), reconcile (to restore friendly relations), deteriorate (to become worse). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ethiopia and Eritrea may go to war again, officials in the region say. If this happens, it will destroy the 2019 peace deal , which ended years of fighting and could make life worse for many people in the Horn of Africa. The problem started after Ethiopia’s civil war in the Tigray region between 2020 and 2022. Eritrea helped Ethiopia fight against the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). After the war, Ethiopia made peace with Tigray, but Eritrea was not part of it. Now, there is a new fight inside Tigray, and Ethiopia and Eritrea may support different sides. Both countries are sending soldiers to the border. Eritrea became independent from Ethiopia in 1993, but they fought again in 1998. They made peace in 2018, but their friendship ended when Ethiopia made a deal with Tigray. Ethiopia also wants sea access , which worries Eritrea. Difficult words: peace deal (when two countries or groups agree to end a war or conflict), civil war (a war between groups within the same country), access (being able to get to or inside a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethiopia and Eritrea might fight again, officials say. If they do, many people in the Horn of Africa will suffer . The problem starts after a war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region. The war starts in 2020 and lasts two years. Eritrea helps Ethiopia fight a group called TPLF. After the war, Ethiopia makes peace with Tigray, but Eritrea is not part of the deal. Now, some people in Tigray are fighting again. Ethiopia and Eritrea may take different sides. Both countries are sending soldiers to the border . Eritrea becomes free from Ethiopia in 1993. They fight again in 1998 but make peace in 2018. Now, they are not friends because Ethiopia makes peace with Tigray. Ethiopia also wants to get to the sea, which Eritrea does not like. Difficult words: suffer (to go through something unpleasant or bad), peace (when there is not a war or conflict), border (the line between two countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Asbestos is a natural mineral that was widely used in construction and industry because of its heat resistance and durability . However, scientists later discovered that asbestos fibers could cause serious lung diseases, such as asbestosis. When asbestos materials are damaged, tiny fibers are released into the air. If inhaled, they can remain in the lungs for years, leading to severe health problems. Many countries have banned asbestos, but older buildings may still contain it. People working in construction, demolition, or renovation must be careful to avoid exposure . Wearing protective equipment and using special removal procedures help reduce the risk. Unfortunately, in some developing countries, asbestos is still used because it is cheap and effective. Experts warn that continued exposure will cause long-term health crises. Governments and health organizations are working to raise awareness and remove asbestos safely. If people suspect asbestos in their homes, they should contact professionals rather than trying to remove it themselves. Difficult words: durability (how long something lasts without breaking), exposure (being in contact with something harmful), awareness (knowledge of a situation or fact). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Asbestos is a mineral that workers used in buildings because it was strong and it didn’t burn. Later, people found out that breathing in asbestos fibers can cause serious lung diseases. These small fibers can stay in the air and get into the lungs, which can cause problems many years later. Many countries don’t allow the use of asbestos anymore, but some old houses and factories still have it. Workers who repair or destroy these buildings must be very careful. They should wear protective clothing and follow safety rules. In some countries, people still use asbestos because it is cheap. Health experts say asbestos is very dangerous and workers must remove it safely. If people think their house has asbestos, they should call professionals instead of touching it themselves. Difficult words: fibers (a very thin piece of material or substance), protective (keeping something safe), remove (to take away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Asbestos is a strong material. It is in houses and many old buildings. People use it because it does not burn. After many years, people find out that asbestos is very dangerous. Small pieces go into the air and can make people sick. If people breathe these pieces, they can have lung problems. Many countries stop using asbestos, but some old buildings still have it. When workers who repair or break buildings they must be careful . They wear special clothes and work safely. Some countries still use asbestos because it is cheap. Doctors say that asbestos is bad for health. If people think they have asbestos at home, they should not touch it. They should call experts to take it away safely. Difficult words: breathe (to take air into the body), lung (one of the two organs which we need to breathe), careful (trying hard not to do anything wrong or damage something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA reported that global sea levels rose more than expected in 2024. Scientists had predicted an increase of 0.43 cm, but instead, it reached 0.59 cm. This rise was mainly due to the warming of the oceans and melting glaciers. 2024 was also the hottest year on record, with global temperatures 1.6°C higher than in pre-industrial times. Experts warn that the speed of sea level rise is increasing, which could lead to serious consequences. Around two-thirds of the surge was caused by thermal expansion , where warmer water takes up more space. Meanwhile, melting glaciers and ice sheets contributed to the remaining third. Climate policies are crucial , but international efforts remain inconsistent . While some countries, like China, are investing in clean energy, others, such as the US, have weakened regulations. The situation is complex , but experts stress that global cooperation is necessary to slow down climate change and its effects. Difficult words: thermal expansion (the increase in the volume of a material as its temperature is increased), crucial (extremely important or necessary), inconsistent (not staying the same), complex (consisting of many different parts). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA says sea levels rose more than expected in 2024. Scientists thought they would rise by 0.43 cm, but they increased by 0.59 cm. This happened because ocean water got warmer and more glaciers melted . 2024 was also the hottest year ever recorded, with temperatures 1.6°C higher than in the past. About two-thirds of the sea level rise happened because warm water expand ed, and melting ice caused the rest. Some countries are trying to use clean energy, but others, like the US, are reducing climate rules. Scientists say countries need to work together to stop the problem. If temperatures keep rising, sea levels will go up even faster, which could be dangerous for people living near the ocean. Difficult words: expect (to think or believe something will happen), melt (when ice or snow turns into water), expand (to get bigger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA says that sea levels go up more than scientists hope. In 2024, they believe the water will rise 0.43 cm. But it rises 0.59 cm. This happens because the ocean gets very hot and ice melts . 2024 is also the hottest year ever. The warm ocean water needs more space . Also, ice from mountains and cold places melts into the sea. Some countries want to stop this problem, but others are not helping. If the Earth gets hotter, the sea will rise more. This can be bad for people who live near the ocean. Scientists say that countries must work together to stop this from happening. Around 100 film projects were submitted to the Impact Days program at the Geneva International Film Festival and Forum on Human Rights, but only 12 were selected. One of them is Children of Honey, a documentary about Tanzania’s Hadzabe people and their fight to preserve their language. The Hadzabe are one of the world’s oldest hunter-gatherer tribes, struggling between keeping their traditions and adapting to modern life. Co-director Jigar Ganatra explained that the Hadza want the world to hear their story and to change how they are portrayed . At the festival, filmmakers present their work to funders and organizations interested in the issues in their films. Impact producer Simona Nickmanova said the team is working closely with the Hadza to support grassroots efforts to protect their language and habitat. All selected filmmakers share a common goal: to use film as a tool for social change. Difficult words: preserve (to keep safe or as it is), hunter-gatherer (people who live by hunting and collecting food), portrayed (represented or described). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Rodrigo Duterte, the former president of the Philippines, was arrested after arriving in Manila from Hong Kong. He was later sent to The Hague because the International Criminal Court (ICC) had issued a warrant for his arrest. The court accuses him of crimes against humanity due to the thousands of killings linked to his war on drugs. These deaths happened when he was the mayor of Davao City and later as the country’s president. Many human rights organizations believe this is an important moment for justice . However, Duterte’s lawyers argue that the ICC has no right to arrest him, as the Philippines left the court in 2019. They have also asked for his return. Meanwhile, his supporters are preparing to protest against his arrest. This case will likely have a big impact on the country. It has already deepened divisions between those who see Duterte as a strong leader and those who blame him for serious human rights abuses. Difficult words: warrant (an official document allowing an arrest), humanity (all people in the world), justice (fair treatment by law), division (difference or disagreement between two or more groups). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: former (happening in the past but not now), responsible (being the reason why something happened), supporter (someone who likes an idea, group, or person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Manchester United have announced plans to build a new 100,000-seat stadium, which will be the largest in the UK. They aim to create the world’s greatest stadium expected to generate 7.3 billion pounds annually for the UK economy. The project will be part of a major regeneration of the Old Trafford area, bringing 92,000 jobs and 17,000 homes. The club’s co-owner, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, stated that the current stadium has served well for 115 years but has fallen behind top venues . By building next to the existing site, they can preserve Old Trafford’s history while creating a modern stadium. The project will also drive long-term investment in the area. The government supports infrastructure growth, especially in northern England, and the club sees this as an opportunity to build a stadium that matches Manchester United’s status. They hope the stadium will become an iconic landmark, similar to famous venues like Wembley or the Eiffel Tower. Difficult words: regeneration (making an area better and more modern), venue (the place where something happens), iconic (widely recognized and well-established). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Copper is often called Dr. Copper because its price is a good indicator of the global economy’s health. This year, its price has risen nearly 14%, which usually suggests strong economic growth and increased industrial demand, especially from China. The country has been introducing measures to support consumption. However, the situation is more complex due to trade tensions between the US, China, and Europe. A key factor is the price difference between domestic and UK copper, which reached a record 920 dollars per metric ton on February 10th before falling to 816 dollars by February 28th. While still high, this is far from its peak. Historically, this difference has ranged between 250 and 500 dollars. The unusually high premium may indicate ongoing trade conflicts rather than a strong global economy. Investors are uncertain whether the recent price increase is a positive signal or just temporary. Difficult words: indicator (a sign or signal that shows something exists or is true), complex (consisting of many different and connected parts), premium (the extra amount paid on something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Experts sometimes call copper Dr. Copper because its price can show how strong the global economy is. This year, copper prices are up nearly 14%. This would normally mean the economy is getting better and industries, especially in China, need more copper. China has plans to help people buy more things, but trade problems between the US, China, and Europe make the situation less clear. The price difference between local copper and UK copper was 920 dollars per metric ton on February 10th but dropped to 816 dollars by February 28th. This is still high, but not as much as before. In the past, the difference was between 250 and 500 dollars. This big difference might be because of trade problems, not a strong economy. Right now, investors are not sure if copper’s price is a good sign. Difficult words: copper (a red-brown metal), metric ton (1,000 kilograms), investor (a person or company who puts money into something to make more money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: wire (a piece of thin metal), difference (how different things are), metric ton (1,000 kilograms). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New tariffs on imports from Canada, Mexico, and China are affecting businesses and consumers. President Trump introduced a 25% tax on most goods from Canada and Mexico, while tariffs on Chinese goods doubled to 20%. These changes may increase prices for everyday items. Experts say businesses are already adjusting their supply chains . Farmers, for example, rely on Canada for fertilizer and Mexico for produce like avocados and tomatoes. With higher import costs, restaurant owners and retailers may pass these costs on to customers. Some companies, especially smaller businesses, may struggle to adapt. During the pandemic, many businesses learned to diversify suppliers. However, these new tariffs present fresh challenges. As prices rise, consumers may spend less, affecting businesses and workers. Trump argues tariffs will strengthen the US economy but admits they may cause short-term disruptions. Difficult words: supply chain (steps in making and delivering products), fertilizer (a substance added to soil or land to improve growth of plants), diversify (use different sources). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some companies can react to these changes, but small businesses may have problems. During the COVID-19 pandemic, businesses learned to use different suppliers . But these tariffs create new problems. If prices go up, people may spend less, which will hurt businesses and jobs. Trump says tariffs will help the country but may also cause problems. Difficult words: add (to put something with something else to make something go up), fertilizer (a substance which makes plants grow better), supplier (a person or company which sells things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Humans have caused the extinction of species like the great auk and pushed many others, such as orangutans and hedgehogs, to the brink . The great auk, a flightless seabird, was hunted for food, feathers, and oil, disappearing completely in 1844. This tragedy helped scientists realize that human actions can drive species to extinction. Today, deforestation, pollution, and climate change are causing a sixth mass extinction. Over a million species are at risk, with entire ecosystems collapsing. The humble hedgehog, for example, is disappearing due to urban expansion, pesticides , and habitat loss. In 2022, countries pledged to protect 30% of the planet by 2030. Individuals like Hotlin Ompusunggu, an Indonesian dentist, have also made a difference. She offers low-cost treatment to those who protect forests, which helps save orangutans. To prevent mass extinction, governments, businesses, and individuals must work together. Difficult words: brink (the edge), pesticide (a substance used for destroying insects or other organisms harmful to cultivated plants or animals), habitat (the natural home or environment of an animal or plant). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some people, like Indonesian dentist Hotlin Ompusunggu, are also helping. Those who protect forests and save orangutans get cheaper care. To stop extinctions, we all need to do something now. Difficult words: feathers (soft and light things that cover a bird’s body), extinction (when animals or plants are gone forever), species (a group of animals or plants). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2015, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau promised to improve Canada’s relationship with Indigenous people and reduce their high imprisonment rates. However, the situation has worsened. Indigenous people, who make up only 5% of Canada’s population, now represent over a third of those under strict supervision after prison. Marvin Starblanket, an Indigenous man from Saskatoon, has spent much of his life in prison due to violent crimes. Currently, he is under a five-year supervision order, restricting his movements, housing, and employment. These orders, meant for rare cases, disproportionately affect Indigenous people. Many face parole denials and strict conditions, increasing their incarceration rates. The causes include poverty, trauma, and lack of opportunities. While some believe supervision provides support, others argue it limits freedom. Starblanket now focuses on his family and hopes to study psychology and advocate for Indigenous rights after his order ends in 2027. He fears the challenge of adjusting to true independence. Difficult words: disproportionately (too much or too little compared to others), parole (early release from prison), incarceration (imprisonment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: violent (hurting people), supervision order (when the court controls someone’s actions), freedom (being free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bhutan has begun constructing a new city near the Indian border to boost its economy and stop the increasing loss of skilled workers. The Prime Minister believes this project could raise Bhutan’s population to three million. The city, named Galu Mindfulness City (GMC), is being built on 25,000 square kilometers of land as a special administrative region. Bhutan aims to create an eco-friendly and safe city, attracting only selected investors. Essential infrastructure is being upgraded, including border crossings, while India is working on a cross-border railway to improve access. The city will focus on sustainability, using hydroelectric power and traditional Bhutanese values. The project is expected to take 21 years, and its vision is based on happiness, well-being, and mindfulness. Many Bhutanese hope GMC will bring prosperity , better roads, and an international airport, significantly improving their country’s economy. The government remains committed to maintaining its cultural values while promoting growth. Difficult words: boost (to help or encourage something to increase or improve), essential (necessary), prosperity (success and wealth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
